    Sheet Pan Pancakes with Greek Yogurt

    Published Nov 24, 2026 · Modified Nov 24, 2026 · by Alexis Joseph, MS, RD · 2 Comments

    Jump to Recipe
    Pin Recipe
    5 from 1 review
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 4:05
    Instaread

    Skip the flip with my easiest nourishing sheet pan pancakes (from a mix)! Trust me when I say this is the breakfast shortcut you didn't know you needed. Made with a healthy pancake mix, protein-packed Greek yogurt, eggs, and olive oil, they're naturally gluten free and surprisingly fluffy. Perfect for busy mornings or meal prep, they're also a top request in my kids lunchboxes! in my kids ask them in their lunchbox! On the table in just 25 minutes.

    The sister recipe to my beloved sheet pan pancakes with cottage cheese, this is the recipe you reach for when you need a wholesome breakfast like yesterday but have zero patience for measuring flour. So fast! So fluffy! So filling!

    So perfectly pancakey, minus the stovetop idling. And those gorgeous ruby lower sugar cranberry sauce swirls? I can't.

    We're going rogue today and totally ignoring the directions on the box. Instead of water (boring!), we're supercharging them with Greek yogurt for serious staying power. Hubba hubba!

    The low down on key ingredients

    • I developed this recipe specifically with Simple Mills Pancake Mix (not sponsored!) on purpose because it's my absolute fave of all the mixes I've tried and one I always keep in the pantry. Since it's made with almond flour, it's naturally higher in fat, so you don't need much extra. I recommend sticking with this mix for best results!
    • Like so many of my nourishing breakfast recipes, I'm leaning into greek yogurt! It makes these SO much better than water. It was clear in testing it adds 10/10 fluff factor, plus who could resist that protein boost?
    • I tested this recipe with both two eggs and three eggs and actually preferred the extra height structure with three eggs.
    • Most pancakes call for melted butter, but I'm an EVOO girlie through and through. Low and behold, it works beautifully in these pancakes too! Be still, my polyphenol loving heart.

    Let's make 'em!

    Nutrition goodies

    As an RD mama of two little boys, I can't help but love that these have over 12.5g of protein and 2.5g of fiber per serving, all whole food ingredients, plus plenty of healthy fats!

    They're also such a fab canvas for adding berries or whatever mix-in's your little heart desires.

    I hope these become an a.m. staple for your fam like it has for mine!

    Sheet Pan Pancakes with Greek Yogurt (from a mix!)

    5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star 5 from 1 review
    • Author: Alexis Joseph, MS, RD
    • Prep Time: 10 minutes
    • Cook Time: 15 minutes
    • Total Time: 25 minutes
    • Yield: 4 servings 1x
    • Method: Baking
    • Cuisine: American
    • Diet: Gluten-Free
    Print Recipe
    Save Recipe Recipe Saved

    Description

    Skip the flip with my easiest sheet pan pancakes (from a mix)! Trust me when I say this is the breakfast shortcut you didn't know you needed. Made with a healthy pancake mix, protein-packed Greek yogurt, eggs, and olive oil, they're naturally gluten free and surprisingly fluffy. Perfect for busy mornings or meal prep, they're also a top request in my kids lunchboxes! in my kids ask them in their lunchbox! On the table in just 25 minutes.

    Ingredients

    Units Scale
    • 1-10.7 oz box Simple Mills Almond Flour Pancake Mix
    • 1 cup plain Greek yogurt
    • 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
    • 3 large eggs
    • 1 tsp vanilla extract
    • toppings of choice: swirls of lower sugar cranberry sauce, fresh or frozen berries, mini chocolate chips, PB&J swirls

    Instructions

    1. Preheat oven to 400°F. Spray a half sheet sheet with cooking spray (I like to line with parchment paper for easy clean up).
    2. In a large mixing bowl, whisk Greek yogurt, eggs, olive oil, and vanilla extract.
    3. Add pancake mix and whisk just until smooth. It will be very thick!
    4. Use a rubber spatula to dump batter onto baking sheet and spread into an even rectangle, about ½ inch thick. It won't cover the whole pan and it will come out about the same size as it goes in. If you fancy, add dollops of cranberry sauce (or jelly) and swirl with a knife. Or dot with chocolate chips/blueberries!
    5. Bake about 15 minutes, until center is set. Cool and devour! My kids love them with whipped cream on top.

    Notes

    Store leftovers in the fridge for up to 3 days. These freeze great, too!
